notes:
Summary: Aegis is a mid-to-large fintech looking to run Redwood Private in their AWS VPC with strict key custody and audit controls. Primary ask: full control of CMKs and tamper-evident audit trail. High sensitivity to plaintext token exposure.

Recent timeline:
- 2025-11-05: Initial intro (Jordan) — basic fit confirmed (latency <120ms, high throughput during market hours).
- 2025-12-08: Discovery call with infra sec (Emily Bauer) — walked through high-level VPC architecture. Emily: "We will not allow any public control-plane endpoints."
- 2026-01-15: Security questionnaire returned (SOC2 + ISO evidence requested).
- 2026-01-22: Follow-up on KMS options (customer CMKs vs Redwood-managed).
- 2026-02-10: Architecture review (ff-2026-02-10-001) — agreed to POC in dev VPC with customer-managed keys.
- 2026-02-20: Network prep email thread (thread-1683022-poc-setup) — customer to provide allowlist and terraform for private endpoints.

Encryption & key management requirements (detailed):
- In-transit: mTLS enforced between control plane agents and inference nodes. TLS 1.3 required; no TLS 1.2 fallback. Mutual auth: customer CA or internal PKI.
- Private endpoints: All endpoints inside VPC; use VPC endpoints / PrivateLink. No public IPs on inference instances.
- At-rest: All volumes, DBs, and object storage must use customer-managed CMKs (AWS KMS). Persistent volumes encrypted server-side with CMK; snapshots/encrypted AMIs also under CMK.
- Envelope encryption: Application-level envelope encryption recommended for model weights and sensitive caches; Redwood to support envelope with customer CMK wrapping data keys.
- Key rotation: Customer policy requires rotation every 90 days for data-encryption keys, yearly rotation for root CMKs. Rotation must be auditable.
- HSM: Customer prefers CloudHSM-backed keys for root-key material; explore external HSM for FIPS-140-2 compliance (legal asks for HSM proof).
- Cross-account grants: Need explicit KMS grants and IAM role assumption pattern (principal: redwood-controlplane@redwood-account). Legal needs a template for KMS grant wording.
- Secrets management: Integration with HashiCorp Vault (preferred) + AWS Secrets Manager fallback. Short lived tokens for agent provisioning; no long lived secrets in plaintext.
- Key usage audit: All KMS GenerateDataKey/Decrypt calls must be logged to CloudTrail and forwarded to customer SIEM (Kafka collector). Retention: 7 years for audit entries; tamper-evident storage required.
- Backup/DR keys: Separate CMKs per region; cross-region replication only after key replication policies approved.

POC scope & milestones (customer dev VPC):
- Milestone 1: Provide VPC & subnet details + allowlist (customer) — expected by 2026-03-05.
- Milestone 2: Deploy control plane inside customer VPC (no public egress) — Redwood to provide terraform modules.
- Milestone 3: Integrate CMK (customer-managed) and validate envelope encryption for model artifacts. Test: upload encrypted artifact, verify decrypt via KMS grants.
- Milestone 4: mTLS handshake proof — generate certs from customer CA, rotate client cert, verify metrics/logging.
- Milestone 5: Audit log pipeline — CloudTrail -> Kinesis -> SIEM, retention verification.
- Milestone 6: Performance test during busy-window (simulate production traffic). Validate latency SLOs and cost estimates.

Customer quotes / notes from calls:
- CTO (Nisha Patel): "We must retain full control of keys and be able to revoke access immediately. No black box key handling."
- Infra Sec (Emily Bauer): "We need signed, immutable logs and proof of key-use. Provide a runbook for incident response."

Open questions / blockers for Redwood sales/eng:
- Can Redwood support CloudHSM-backed CMKs or provide an HSM integration guide?
- KMS cross-account grant process: need legal-approved template for customer to sign.
- Secrets onboarding: customer wants Vault integration pattern (AppRole + short TTL). Provide sample HashiCorp config.
- Network egress: customer requires static egress IPs for outbound KMS requests. Engineering to confirm feasibility.
- SLA & liability clauses around key compromise in contract (legal input required).

Next steps (concrete):
- Schedule 90-min security deep-dive with Redwood infra security (Emily + Maya + Jordan + customer security) — aim week of 2026-03-08.
- Deliver KMS policy template + example Terraform module for CMK grants by 2026-03-04 (action: Maya).
- Share Vault AppRole example and short-lived token provisioning guide (action: Redwood DevX).
- Open Jira INF-4592 to track POC infra tasks; SEC-3138 for security evidence collection.

Short notes (CRM style):
- High priority: data residency + key custody.
- Decision criteria: KMS/HSM support, audit/log forwarding, private-only endpoints.
- Procurement timeline: legal + procurement aiming for June close if POC OK.
- Quote: "No plaintext tokens in our VPC" — translate to policy enforcement.
